does: Fries a thick seasoning paste, such as a chilli bean paste or a curry paste, slowly in fat until it smells rich and the fat takes its colour, before any liquid goes in.
how: Heat a little oil, or the thick cream from the top of a tin of coconut milk, over medium heat.
For coconut cream, let it bubble until it starts to split and look oily.
Add the paste and fry it, stirring and scraping, over a gentle heat.
Stop when it smells rich and the fat around it has turned red, then add the liquid.

cues.text: The raw, sharp smell turns deep and fragrant.
The fat separates and turns red around the paste.

mistakes.mistake: Frying the paste over high heat, so it burns before it gives up its flavour.
mistakes.fix: Keep the heat medium or low and keep stirring.

mistakes.mistake: Adding the liquid at once, which leaves a raw, flat taste.
mistakes.fix: Fry the paste until the fat is red first.
